title: SO-F-04A Composition of the checks on the Admission external hook: one function of the shape the hook takes that runs the relationship check of SO-F-04 and any other check, such as the admission adapter of SO-F-08, in the order given, a refusal beating a degraded answer, and nothing added to the steps or events of the Admission
request: Follow-up to the signed SO-F-04, written from the open follow-up row 'Two users of the Admission external hook' of docs/scope-one/RECONCILIATION.md (relationshipGate of SO-F-04, pull request #368, and SO-F-08). Unsigned: a delta proposed for red-team review. It does not supersede SO-F-04 or SO-F-08 and does not edit them: SO-F-04 keeps its ten criteria and SO-F-08 keeps its nine, and this contract adds one function and the rules for composing checks. The id has no '.N' suffix because in this repository a '.N' id (SO-F-03.2, SO-F-09.2) is a superseding version; this is an additive follow-up, as SO-W-08C is to SO-W-08B. BASE: SO-F-04. The files this contract names exist only in pull request #368 (head 042d727: src/engine/federation/policy.mjs with relationshipGate, src/engine/federation/membership.mjs, test/helpers/federation-node.mjs) and in pull request #358 (SO-F-03.3: src/engine/federation/admission.mjs, whose constructor takes the optional external check), which is stacked under it. Neither is merged. Draft, red-team and sign this contract against a base that holds them, and build it after they merge; on main today the named test cannot load its helper and the check cannot run. This pull request is spec only. WHAT THE CODE DOES TODAY (read at 042d727): the external option of Admission is one optional synchronous function of the envelope that returns { ok: true } or { ok: false, code, reason }; it runs after the format step and before the signature, authority and replay steps; a refusal, a result that is not { ok: true } and a throw are each appended as federation.rejected with step external (a throw with the code external_failed), with nothing of the payload. relationshipGate returns a function of that shape. There is no way to hold two checks. SO-F-08 (signed, no code on main or on any branch of this repository) asks for an external admission service that runs before the node's own admission and before any append, and, when the service is unavailable, for degraded admission to be reported and the contribution to be queued and not admitted; the hook has no answer for 'unavailable' and treats it as a refusal. WHAT THIS CONTRACT SPECIFIES: composeExternal(...checks), exported from src/engine/federation/admission.mjs, returns one function of the hook's shape. Checks run in the order given. A check that returns { ok: true } passes. A check that returns { ok: false, degraded: true, code, reason } could not decide (the service is unavailable). Anything else that is not a pass, a throw, and a value that is not an object are refusals. The first refusal ends the run and is the answer, and no later check is called. A degraded answer is remembered and the later checks still run, so a definite refusal by the node's own check outranks an unavailable service whatever the order; if nothing refuses and something was degraded, the first degraded answer is the answer; if every check passes, the answer is { ok: true }. An empty list passes and leaves the Admission's events as they are without the option. The Admission gains no step, code or event; how it handles a degraded answer (queue it, report it) is SO-F-08 and is not specified here, and until then a degraded answer admits nothing. BOUNDARIES: (1) PG-W-21B (on main since pull request #371, unsigned, not to be signed before the owner signs off ADR 8) also describes a composeExternal in task WP21-03, in src/engine/federation/trust-gate.mjs, with the same ordering and throw rules and without the degraded answer; the two must not both define it. This contract proposes to own it, because both users the register row names need it and neither needs trust; WP21-03 would then cite it. That is an owner question, listed in the pull request, and PG-W-21B is not edited here. ADR 8 (proposed) says a trust check that cannot run refuses, so a throw is a refusal here and nothing in this contract gives a trust check a degraded answer; the degraded answer is for the admission service of SO-F-08. (2) The trust adapter boundary is WP09-02 of PG-09.1 and the admission adapter is SO-F-08; this contract builds neither, and its tests use stand-in checks, not an SO-F-08 module that does not exist. (3) The hook stays synchronous. An admission service with a timeout (SO-F-08) is a call that may need to be asynchronous; whether the hook or the adapter changes for that is an owner question and not decided here. (4) A signed contribution proves a key signed it; the composed check still skips no later step, so signature, authority and replay run after a pass. Provenance: written for this repository, not adapted from the fold. Settled decisions this contract follows (owner decision 31 Oct 2026, docs/scope-one/DECISIONS.md): topology is local-first and the cloud is only a relay and a backup; every supported provider stands on equal footing and no work or tier depends on one; crdt-merge is reached only through the provider boundary of src/engine/merge.mjs and this contract adds no merge engine to the core (ADR 6, decided); tiers follow docs/PRICING.md and federation stays a planned capability of the tiers above Personal, by contacting us, never a price cell. Open decisions this contract does not make: ADR 7 (memory and project-state authority, proposed) is cited and not decided, and this contract adds no store and no event type beyond the two the Admission already writes (federation.admitted and federation.rejected), so there is one store under the vault and no second database; ADR 2 (id and event ordering, open) keeps its safe default, the order of the operation log, and this contract adds no sequence of its own; ADR 3 (lease semantics, open) and ADR 5 (permission matrix, open) are not touched, and nothing here is a lease or a role-by-action rule. ADR 8 (trust governance in the federated model, proposed, pending owner decision; docs/scope-one/DECISIONS.md and docs/scope-one/design/trust-governance.md) is not decided or pre-empted: nothing here defines a trust record, a trust gate, who may grant trust or how a revocation propagates, and no criterion reads trust.

tasks.title: SO-F-04A Composition of the checks on the Admission external hook: one function of the shape the hook takes that runs the relationship check of SO-F-04 and any other check, such as the admission adapter of SO-F-08, in the order given, a refusal beating a degraded answer, and nothing added to the steps or events of the Admission
requirements: composeExternal(...checks), exported from src/engine/federation/admission.mjs, returns one function of the shape the external option of Admission takes, and runs the checks in the order given

the first refusal is the answer and no later check is called; a check that throws, that returns a value which is not an object, or that returns anything other than { ok: true } or a degraded answer is a refusal, and a throw has a code of its own, external_check_failed

a degraded answer ({ ok: false, degraded: true }) is remembered and the later checks still run; a refusal beats a degraded answer whatever the order, and with no refusal the first degraded answer is the answer

an empty list passes, and an Admission given it appends the same events as an Admission with no external option; a non-function entry is a TypeError when the composition is made, and the list is copied then
relationshipGate of SO-F-04 and a stand-in for the SO-F-08 service compose in either order with no change to the steps, codes or events of the Admission, and a degraded answer admits nothing
docs/FEDERATION.md states the composition rule and that the order is the node's, with local checks before a call to a service
tasks.description: The Admission of SO-F-03.3 takes one optional check, and two things need it: the relationship check of SO-F-04 and the external admission service of SO-F-08. This contract gives a node a way to hold both without changing the Admission: one function that runs a list of checks and answers in the hook's own shape. It also gives the hook the one answer the service needs and the hook lacks, 'could not decide', and fixes what that answer does next to a definite refusal, so a node never queues a contribution that its own rules refuse. It specifies no service, no trust check and no transport, and it changes no step of the Admission. The named test imports each module of the contract by namespace (import * as ns), never by name, and asserts that the export it needs is a function or a class before it uses it, so that on the base the red run fails on an assertion; the red-green check treats a load error as BLOCKED, not as red.

criteria.statement: composeExternal is a function exported from src/engine/federation/admission.mjs and returns one function of the shape the Admission external option takes: it runs the checks in the order given, answers with the first refusal (its code and reason, and the position of the check), and does not call a later check; a throw, a value that is not an object and a result other than { ok: true } are each a refusal, a throw with the code external_check_failed; a non-function entry is a TypeError when the composition is made and a later change to the caller's list has no effect; the test fails by assertion on the base

criteria.statement: a degraded answer ({ ok: false, degraded: true, code, reason }) is carried through unchanged with the position of its check; the checks after it still run; a refusal beats a degraded answer in either order and the refusal's own code is the answer; with no refusal the first of several degraded answers is the answer; with every check passing the answer is { ok: true }; a check that throws is never taken for degraded

criteria.statement: Every changed file is inside this contract's scope

stop_rules: Stop and post BLOCKED when a criterion cannot pass without weakening a test, skipping a test or relaxing an assertion.
Stop and ask when the work would name a client product, a person, a server or a seat in repository text; the client names live in docs/CLIENTS.md only.
Stop when the work would add a runtime dependency, a model call, a network call at install or start, a second store for project state, or any reporting that is not opt-in and off by default.
Stop when the work would move convergence logic into the core, vendor the engine, or add a merge engine beside the provider boundary of src/engine/merge.mjs.

Stop when the work would implement a federation, replication, trust, admission or computation feature beyond the specification, schema, validator and conformance test the contract names; the product keeps the planned label on it.

Stop and ask when the work would change a step, a code or an event type of the Admission, edit a file of SO-F-03.3 beyond adding the one export, or define how the Admission handles a degraded answer: that is SO-F-08.

Stop and ask when the work would define a trust record, a trust check or the place of one in the order, or would decide any open ADR (ADR 8 above all); the trust gate belongs to its own contract and waits for the owner.
Stop and ask when the work would make the hook asynchronous, add a call to a service, a timer or a clock of its own, or add a second definition of composeExternal beside the one this contract names.
If any criterion fails after the fix: STOP, report the measured result, the failing check and file:line. Do not start the next task.
If the work needs a path outside scope: STOP and ask the owner to amend the contract. Never widen scope silently.
